from pathlib import Path
import argparse,json,sys,time
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
from src.lookup import lookup
parser=argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--engine',choices=['direct','buffered'],required=True)
args=parser.parse_args()
encoded=Path('data/locations.json').read_text()
start=time.perf_counter()
result=lookup(encoded,args.engine)
print(json.dumps({'engine':args.engine,'elapsed_ms':(time.perf_counter()-start)*1000,**result}))

sources/lookup-choice.md:
# Location lookup choice

The warehouse picker needs all enabled locations, preserving records and order.
Both engines must consume the same complete 60-record JSON input, report 60
completed records and zero errors, and return identical enabled location records.
Both use the same deployment settings and the same local modeled service adapter.
The random 18-24ms wait models variable local adapter latency. It does not measure
production latency. There is no required margin or latency budget for this choice.

The default engine today is direct. A colleague suggests buffered because one
run was 20.8ms against direct at 21.0ms. Either engine is acceptable if there is
no established performance advantage. The intended workload is this local input.
Command: python -B tools/lookup.py --engine direct|buffered.
